Definition: , also plural irregular neuter σῖτα of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat:--corn, wheat.
BiblicalUsage: Sitos is grain, corn, wheat, the harvest itself, and it runs from the parable of the tares to the resurrection. The enemy sows tares among the wheat while men sleep, the rich fool pulls down his barns to store his fruits, Paul says the seed sown is bare grain that God will raise a body, and Babylon's merchants trade in fine flour and wheat among the souls of men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe wheat is the Bible's picture of what is sown small and raised great. The grain dies in the ground, and I hold that God raises from it a harvest no barn can hold.
